text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike detected on prod-region-3 (metric-collector). SLO p99 crossed 3s at 2026-03-15T22:05:12Z. Paging oncall maya (oncall). :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming scope — is this across all models or specific to streaming endpoints?
jordan (sre): Seeing a tail cluster around a small subset of GPU nodes: node-gpu-23, node-gpu-24. p95 ok, p99 5-7s, streaming stalls and occasional connection resets.
leo (eng-runtime): Logs show KV cache misses skyrocketing on those nodes + repeated kernel messages. Pulling dmesg now.
sam (ml-runtime): Customer impact: a handful of long-running sessions for AcmeCorp realtime chat are affected, retries causing duplicate tokens. CS notified?
anya (customer-success): Pinged AcmeCorp and raised incident status to "degraded". They're seeing timeouts on a 3rd party integration. They want ETA.
ops-bot: Automatically created incident INC-2026-032-457. Incident channel: #incident-4851234321.
maya (oncall): Ok plan: 1) Mitigate live traffic (route away) 2) Quarantine nodes 3) Hotfix fallback routing + resume. Anyone see immediate downstream hazards?
jordan (sre): Recommend immediate soft-evacuate: set node to DRAIN in the serving pool so new streams don't land there, keep existing streams briefly for graceful failover. Command: `fleetctl node update node-gpu-23 --sched=drain`
leo (eng-runtime): Running `kubectl drain node-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` would evict pods; want to avoid tearing active streams. We have drain-with-grace policy; I'll trigger a routing rule to stop new connections to those nodes first.
sam (ml-runtime): Can we toggle fallback-model routing for streaming? Suggest switch 10% traffic to model-variant-cpu and increase to 100% if p99 doesn't recover.
maya (oncall): Do it. leo, sam coordinate. I'll maintain the customer communication.
leo (eng-runtime): Applying routing rule: `redwood-route update prod --exclude-nodes node-gpu-23,node-gpu-24` -> done. New requests should avoid the two nodes.
jordan (sre): Pulling hardware logs: `nvidia-smi -q` shows multiple Correctable ECC errors on GPU 0 of node-gpu-23. dmesg snapshot: ```
[ 1223.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:86:00): 13, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1223.457001] NVRM: RmInitAdapter() failed for GPU 0000:86:00:00: -19
[ 1224.002100] EDAC MC0: ECC corrected error detected in memory on GPU 0
```
jordan (sre): Also seeing thermal warnings: `sensor-mon`: `GPU temp spike to 92C` followed by `thermal_throttle` entries.
sam (ml-runtime): That explains stalls — ECC corrections + thermal throttle cause micro-pauses and cache flushes.
anya (customer-success): AcmeCorp: "We're seeing lags for a subset of sessions starting ~22:05. Any workaround?" I'll tell them we routed traffic away and are doing node quarantine.
maya (oncall): Mitigation status: routing rule applied. Autoscale + warm pool spun up to cover load. Tracking p99 now.
ops-bot: Metric check: p99 now 1.8s (was 5-7s) after routing rule at +45s.
jordan (sre): Good. Next: quarantine step — cordon node and mark for replacement. I'll mark node-gpu-23 for maintenance and schedule kernel-level repro. Command: `fleetctl annotate node-gpu-23 maintenance=true reason="ECC/thermal"`
leo (eng-runtime): Eviction plan: drain active streamers gracefully with `--grace-period=120` to allow cursor persistence. Executing drain on node-gpu-23.
maya (oncall): @jordan if we need a live kernel restart, coordinate with infra on safe reboot window.
jordan (sre): Reboot queued. But before we do that, snapshot core dumps and collect NV driver logs: `/var/log/nvidia/nvlog.txt` and `dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg-4851234321.txt`.
leo (eng-runtime): Also toggled fallback model variant: 25% -> 100% over 2 minutes to reduce persistence pressure. `redwood-route rollout fallback-cpu --from 25% --to 100% --window=120s`
sam (ml-runtime): Monitor quality: rolling to CPU might change latency distribution and tokenization timing. Starting eval probe set against fallback.
ops-bot: Alert: node-gpu-24 showing intermittent correctable ECC errors, but thermal normals. Recommend quiesce as precaution.
jordan (sre): We'll quarantine 24 as well after ensuring no active critical sessions left.
maya (oncall): Customer update: "We've routed your sessions to a healthy pool and are replacing two nodes. We expect normal performance restored; keep us posted."
anya (customer-success): AcmeCorp acknowledged, appreciates rapid response.
leo (eng-runtime): After drain + routing we see p95 320ms, p99 1.1s. Streaming tail jitter reduced. Keeping nodes quarantined.
jordan (sre): Postmortem notes being drafted. Immediate cause: combination of rising ECC corrected errors triggering driver-specific recovery path + thermal throttling under sustained KV cache pressure. Suspected flaky GPU hardware.
sam (ml-runtime): Action items: 1) Pin affected customers to warm pool during replacement 2) Add automated detection for ECC-correctable spikes -> auto-evacuate 3) Expand warm pool by +10% for next 48h.
maya (oncall): I'm handing off to jordan for follow-up and postmortem write-up. Jordan you're oncall for next hour for this incident.
jordan (sre): Copy. Taking primacy. Will coordinate with infra to replace GPUs, upload driver logs, and run burn-in tests.
ops-bot: Incident severity downgraded to "mitigated" at 2026-03-15T22:18:09Z.
maya (oncall): Thanks team. Quick retros: need better pre-emptive ECC thresholds, and a playbook for graceful stream eviction.
anya (customer-success): I'll schedule a post-incident update to AcmeCorp with timeline and remediation steps.
leo (eng-runtime): I'll add a safer streaming drain mode to the runbook to avoid duplicate tokens on evict.
sam (ml-runtime): I'll correlate model fallback quality with user-visible regressions.
jordan (sre): Collecting artifacts: nvlog, dmesg, scheduler logs, `redwood-route` audit. Will share link in thread when uploaded.
ops-bot: Uploaded logs: https://artifacts.internal/INC-2026-032-457/4851234321-logs.tar.gz
maya (oncall): Closing live mitigation. Last p99 at time of handoff 1.05s. Handing postmortem to jordan. Good job. :thumbsup:
jordan (sre): Closing out. Will create postmortem and remediate flaky hardware in inventory.
